# Genesis Apocryphon Column 20 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Genesis Apocryphon Column 20 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 20:7 — "her nose" / "the curve of her nose"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "how-pleasing is-her-nose" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "how pleasing is her nose" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "how pleasing the curve of her nose" | Dynamic; adds "curve" for physicality |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. PNEUMA's "curve" adds descriptive detail not in the Aramaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:9 — "whiteness" / "fairness" / "luminous skin"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all-her-whiteness" | Literal rendering of Aramaic chuwarha |
| LOGOS | "all her fairness" | Formal; archaic English for beauty/complexion |
| PNEUMA | "her luminous skin" | Dynamic; captures the radiance connotation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted PNEUMA's "luminous skin." The Aramaic chuwarha denotes radiant brightness, not merely paleness. "Whiteness" is misleading in modern English; "fairness" is ambiguous; "luminous skin" best conveys the intended meaning.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of PNEUMA.

---

## 20:10 — "perfect" / "graceful"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "how-perfect" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "how perfect" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "how graceful" | Dynamic; "graceful" suits hands better |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted PNEUMA's "graceful." For hands, "graceful" is more natural and evocative than the abstract "perfect."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of PNEUMA.

---

## 20:12 — "bridal chamber" / "wedding chamber"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-bridal-chamber" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "the bridal chamber" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "the wedding chamber" | Dynamic synonym |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the bridal chamber." This is the more established English term for the ancient institution.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:17 — "one mouth" / "one voice"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as-with-one-mouth" | Literal Aramaic idiom |
| LOGOS | "as with one mouth" | Formal; preserves idiom |
| PNEUMA | "with one voice" | Dynamic; more natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "as with one mouth." The Aramaic idiom is vivid and intelligible in English; there is no need to flatten it.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:18 — "was amazed" / "marveled" / "was stunned"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "was-amazed" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "marveled" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "was stunned" | Dynamic; stronger impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Compromise: "was astonished." This is stronger than "marveled" but less colloquial than "stunned."

**Status:** Resolved as compromise.

---

## 20:22 — "taken from me" / "torn from me"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "was-taken from-me" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "was taken from me" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "had been torn from me" | Dynamic; intensifies the violence |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "was taken from me." The Aramaic verb does not carry the violence of "torn"; the force is indicated separately by "by force."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:30 — "come down upon" / "descend upon" / "strike him down"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "come-down upon" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "descend upon" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "strike him down" | Dynamic; action-oriented |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "descend upon." PNEUMA's "strike down" changes the image from God's hand descending to a blow.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:34 — "pestilential spirit" / "plague-spirit"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-pestilential-spirit" | Literal rendering of rucha mare'ita |
| LOGOS | "a pestilential spirit" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "a plague-spirit" | Dynamic; simpler compound |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "a pestilential spirit." The fuller form preserves the gravity of the Aramaic compound.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 9*
*Resolution: LOGOS 6, PNEUMA 2, Compromise 1, EMET 0*
